text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Tuesday it appeared that "Indonesia-bashing" had become popular among certain groups in the United States.
"I think U.S.-Indonesian relations... government-to-government are quite good," he said at a year-end foreign policy review.

"What is regrettable is in these relations sometimes the views of certain groups, the views of certain persons in Congress, in NGOs (non-governmental organisations) (and) in the press get to the point where they interfere with these relations," he said.
"It's a fashion now to be an Indonesia-basher," he said.
Alatas was responding to a question on the effect on relations between the two countries of election funds made available to the U.S. Democratic Party by some Indonesians.

News reports in the United States have said over $400,000 was donated to the Democratic Party by a couple linked with Indonesia's Lippo Group. The deputy head of the Lippo group is James Riady, a friend of U.S. President Bill Clinton.
"It's silly, it's ridiculous to depict James Riady's contribution as being able to influence, able to sway the policy of the American government," Alatas said.
He added it was also clear "that not only James Riady, but hundreds have given to both parties (Democrats and Republicans)".

Someone, however, wanted to embarrass Indonesia, Alatas said, adding he could only conclude that "there is some sort of campaign going on...(where they) can't stand Indonesia's progress, perhaps, can't stand our system".
He also dismissed congressional opposition to the sale of U.S. F-16 jet fighters to Indonesia.
"We never wanted (them) in the first place, so if (they're) not sold to us, OK, fine," Alatas said.
Washington's sale of F-16s to Pakistan was blocked by Congress and the U.S. government now is trying to sell nine of the jets to Indonesia.
